target: free-search-15: the run-level Holt-Klee obstruction for one-player all-switches, and walk realisation as a linear programme in the value vectors (labels fs15:)
verdict:
EIGHT of the route's nine results are already in frontier.tex, and the ninth is worth one corollary. Integrating the route as written would make the paper WORSE.

WHAT HAPPENED. frontier.tex is now 11838 lines, not the 10856 the route was briefed on. Commit 9fafa72 (2026-09-03 02:53) integrated sec:ties from the concurrently-running round-15 "degenerate" route; the route's own fs15.tex was last written at 02:24. The two routes independently built the same theory. This is not dishonesty by free-search-15 -- it had no way to know -- but the integration decision must treat the overlap as duplication, and it is total:

  fs15:run-hk          = lem:tie-perturb.  The route's hypothesis "0 not in conv{D_{t,v}}" is exactly the Gordan dual of the paper's (star), and the paper SAYS SO ("This is the shape Gordan's alternative predicts: (star) is infeasible exactly when some nonnegative combination of the vectors y^{sigma_t}-y^{sigma_t[v]} vanishes").
  fs15:tie-partner     = the (F1)-(F4) apparatus of lem:seven-flat, plus thm:no-seven's opening ("c_{A(sigma_t)} := sigma_t is a consistent choice of corners").
  the whole premise ("prop:oneplayer-lp uses nondegeneracy only at the end") = sec:ties' second paragraph, verbatim in content.
  |T| <= 1 is free     = cor:one-tie (which is STRONGER: all ties at one vertex with the SAME action).
  fs15:f1-four         = thm:no-seven + cor:hstar-one (STRONGER: h*_1(m) = 1,2,4,6 for m <= 4, both bounds).
  fs15:h12-oneplayer   = the paragraph after prop:hkfive (STRONGER: the whole orbit of s_12, both length-12 starts, not one walk).
  fs15:escape-real     = prop:no-linear-tiebreak (STRONGER: also counts the 96 acyclic completions, 74 Holt-Klee, and confirms L <= h*_HK(4) survives there).
  fs15:nu-half         = two lines from lem:alphabet-cover; the route says so itself.
  fs15:walk-lp         = the design method of prop:b2-realised's proof ("its rows were fixed by exact linear programming over the normal form"), which the gadget route used to SUCCEED on the very instance fs15's outer search failed on.

Even the individual tools are paper-resident: the Szabo-Welzl completion enumeration is prop:hkfive's program, the unit-vertex-capacity Holt-Klee test is cor:seven-two-player's, and h*_HK(5)=11 is now proved (prop:hkfive), not "measured, unverified".

WHAT SURVIVES. fs15:b2-oneplayer, and only that. I rebuilt the enumeration from scratch (independent USO/acyclicity/Holt-Klee/BA-walk library, /tmp/.../audit-fs15-sig/ind.py) and reproduce the route exactly: 1897 USO completions of the B^2 walk, 875 acyclic, ZERO Holt-Klee, legal candidate tie sets exactly {}, {(5,2)}, {(7,3)}, {(5,2),(7,3)} with counts 180/162/297/236; sigma_5 = 17 takes action 0 at bit 2 while sigma_7 = 6 takes action 1, so fs15:two-ties applies. The result is correct, is NOT in the paper, and is NOT reachable by sec:ties' method: B^2's walk has length 10 <= 11 = h*_HK(5), so the height argument gives nothing and the walk-completion screen is genuinely needed. It is now the exact sharpness complement to prop:b2-realised, which realises that walk with FIVE Max and ONE Min: that one Min vertex is necessary, ties allowed. That is the m=5 analogue of what thm:no-seven did for cor:seven-two-player, and it is worth one corollary in sec:ties.

I also independently reproduced the m=4 half (384 orbit outmaps, 768 length-7 pairs, candidate-tie distribution 384 x {one} + 384 x {none}, every discarded candidate having its partner on the walk) -- so fs15:f1-four is correct, just already proved.

THREE THINGS ARE WRONG, none fatal to a conclusion.
(1) fs15:two-ties-cor(ii) is VACUOUS, and fs15:escape-remark's sharpness claim is false. The route reads only the coordinate (v_1, a_1); reading the COMPLEMENTARY coordinate (v_1, 1-a_1) kills case (ii) in one line (see finding). So the route's "dichotomy" is strictly WEAKER than the paper's prose assertion it was meant to sharpen -- prop:no-linear-tiebreak's surrounding text already says the same-vertex-opposite-actions configuration is the only one, and it is right.
(2) fs15:walk-lp claims "Any solution with delta>0 is a stopping game". It is a harmonic normal form, not a game. Rows -> fair-coin SSG is unverified item (v4), and the route's own calibration output (t_gsharp.py) contains the row margin 16360316286458789090051467880599179/2247486763375641182884452430940917760, whose denominator has a 100-bit ODD part -- realising that as a first-passage law of a fair-coin average part needs an eventually-periodic binary expansion of astronomical period. Every realisation in the paper (prop:auso-seven, prop:b2-realised, rem:hk-survey) rounds to a small dyadic denominator and then verifies from the explicit game, precisely because of this.
(3) The stated gap carries a false "equivalently" (see finding).

WHAT IT DOES NOT DO. No algorithm, no polynomial class, no lower-bound family, no barrier: it covers NONE of M1, M2, M2T, M3, M4, M5, M6 or def:bsi. This is the regime rem:flat already describes for the whole AUSO-ceiling programme -- "no bound on any algorithm, no polynomial class, no barrier and no lower-bound family". fs15:top is honestly self-declared as ending at a target-equivalent statement, which by rule 4 is a blocked route, and it is the seventh such reformulation.

HONESTY. Good, in the two places it matters. The sampling (15000 games at m=3, 4000 at m=4) is used only to report the RARITY of a configuration exhibited by an explicit instance, never to support a claim. The failed searches are reported with the calibration control failing and the correct caveat that they are evidence about the search and not about the instances -- and prop:b2-realised, which found the game the route could not, proves that caveat was exactly right.

RECOMMENDATION. Integrate ONE result: fs15:b2-oneplayer, restated inside sec:ties in the paper's own vocabulary (cor:one-tie plus the completion enumeration of prop:hkfive plus the same-vertex-opposite-actions lemma), as a corollary sharpening prop:b2-realised. Optionally add fs15:top as one paragraph to the target-equivalence list (thm:compare-equivalence, thm:decide-one-bit, prop:no-halving, cor:wrong-equivalence, rem:alphabet-equivalence), after deleting the collapsed vertices in the proof. Reject everything else as duplicate. Take from the route's next-steps the ONE item the paper explicitly says its own method cannot reach: the paragraph after prop:hkfive concedes "This does not give h*_1(5) <= 11"; the walk-level screen does, by running the completion+tie test on all 347640 length-12 sequences (about 2900 up to the 120 permutations fixing sigma_0), and that would extend cor:hstar-one to m=5. Also worth doing while the screen is being written: replace fs15:two-ties-cor with the corrected single-case dichotomy, and record the general form the complementary-coordinate reading gives -- at every Max vertex v carrying a tie with action a, either some tie at v with action 1-a carries positive weight, or some tie (t,u) with u != v has sigma_t(v) = 1-a -- which is the first constraint anyone has on tie sets of size >= 3.

findings.defect: All five are already in frontier.tex, integrated at commit 9fafa72 as sec:ties from the concurrently-running round-15 'degenerate' route, and in every case the paper's version is at least as strong. fs15:run-hk is lem:tie-perturb read through Gordan's alternative (which the paper names explicitly); fs15:f1-four is thm:no-seven plus cor:hstar-one, which additionally gives the whole table h*_1(m)=1,2,4,6 for m<=4; fs15:h12-oneplayer is the paragraph following prop:hkfive, which covers the entire orbit of s_12 and both length-12 starts rather than a single walk; fs15:escape-real is prop:no-linear-tiebreak, a 34-vertex one-player game with two flat incidences at one Max vertex with opposite actions and exactly anti-parallel occupancy differences, which additionally enumerates the 96 acyclic completions. Not the route's fault (fs15.tex was written at 02:24, the integration landed at 02:53) but decisive for the integration verdict.
findings.evidence: git log: 9fafa72 2026-09-03 02:53:34 '... sec:ties (the degenerate route) and h*_HK(5)=11 integrated'; ls -la fs15.tex -> 2026-09-03 02:24:48. frontier.tex lines 4926-5270 contain lem:tie-perturb, cor:one-tie, lem:seven-flat, thm:no-seven, cor:hstar-one, prop:hkfive and prop:no-linear-tiebreak. Line ~5165: 'This is the shape Gordan's alternative predicts: (star) is infeasible exactly when some nonnegative combination of the vectors y^{sigma_t}-y^{sigma_t[v]} vanishes, and the smallest way is two flat incidences at the same Max vertex with opposite actions.'

findings.defect: Case (ii) of the dichotomy is vacuous, so the corollary is strictly weaker than the prose claim in frontier.tex it was meant to upgrade, and the accompanying sharpness claim in fs15:escape-remark ('fs15:two-ties is sharp: the only two-tie configuration it leaves open is the one fs15:escape-real exhibits') contradicts the corollary's own statement. The route reads only the coordinate (v_1, a_1), where D_{t_2,v_2} need not vanish; reading the complementary coordinate (v_1, 1-a_1) closes the case in one line.
findings.evidence: Let T={(t1,v1),(t2,v2)} with v1!=v2 and sigma_{t1}(v1)=sigma_{t2}(v1)=a1 (case ii). y^sigma is supported exactly on {(u,sigma(u))} with entries >=1 (prop:oneplayer-lp). At (v1,1-a1): y^{sigma_t1} has 0, y^{sigma_t1[v1]} has >=1, so D_{t1,v1} <= -1 there; sigma_t2 and sigma_t2[v2] both take a1 at v1 (v2!=v1), so D_{t2,v2}=0 there. Then c1 D_1 + c2 D_2 = 0 with c1,c2>=0 forces c1=0, hence c2 D_2=0 with c2>0, hence D_2=0, false. Case (i) survives the same test, as it must (opposite signs at (v,1-a)). Written up at /tmp/claude-1000/-data-ssg-proof/6e64b33d-520c-4c82-aa1b-ffb69ecfcb61/scratchpad/audit-fs15-sig/CASE_II_DEAD.md. Consistent with the route's own report that all three sampled escapes were type (i).

findings.defect: The proposition asserts 'Any solution with delta>0 is a stopping game whose all-switches run from sigma_0 is exactly sigma_0,...,sigma_L'. A solution is a harmonic normal form -- a set of substochastic affine rows -- not a game. Turning arbitrary rational rows into a def:ssg game (fair coins, out-degree two) is unverified item (v4) of the standing list, and the size is unbounded: a non-dyadic row needs an eventually-periodic binary expansion whose period is the multiplicative order of 2 modulo the odd part of the denominator. Every realisation in frontier.tex (prop:auso-seven, prop:b2-realised, rem:hk-survey) instead rounds to a small dyadic denominator and then verifies the outmap from the explicit game -- exactly the step this proposition skips.
findings.evidence: The route's own calibration run, t_gsharp.py, returns per-row margins including 16360316286458789090051467880599179/2247486763375641182884452430940917760; that denominator has odd part 548702823089756148165149519272685 (about 100 bits), so it is not dyadic and is not the first-passage law of any average part of reasonable size. The route calls this output a 'rebuilt game'.

findings.defect: The stated gap contains a false 'equivalently'. Escaping fs15:run-hk requires only that 0 lie in conv{D_{t,v}} over the whole tie set T; fs15:two-ties constrains PAIRS only. With case (ii) dead the |T|=2 analysis is complete, but |T|>=3 is untouched -- Gordan's alternative then needs a nonnegative combination of three or more vectors and no pair need be anti-parallel. So 'a run longer than h*_HK(m)' is not equivalent to 'a type-(i) two-tie configuration on a long run'. The true gap: whether some one-player stopping SSG has an all-switches run of length > h*_HK(m) whose tied incidences on the run carry occupancy differences D_{t,v} = y^{sigma_t} - y^{sigma_t[v]} that positively span 0 -- a tie set of ANY size, not two.
findings.evidence: fs15:two-ties and its corollary are stated for exactly two tied incidences; nothing in the route bounds |T| or handles |T|>=3. frontier.tex states the gap correctly at the end of prop:no-linear-tiebreak's discussion: 'Whether every one-player stopping game satisfies L <= h*_HK(|Vmax|) remains open.'

findings.defect: Not a defect: this is the one result of the route that is new, correct, and worth integrating. It is not reachable by sec:ties' method, since B^2's walk has length 10 <= 11 = h*_HK(5) (prop:hkfive), so the height argument gives nothing and the walk-completion screen is genuinely required. It is now the exact sharpness complement to prop:b2-realised, whose realisation uses five Max and ONE Min vertex: that Min vertex is necessary, degenerate games included.
findings.evidence: Reproduced from scratch with an independently written USO/acyclicity/Holt-Klee/BA-walk library (/tmp/.../audit-fs15-sig/ind.py, calibrated on the paper's height-7 and height-6 4-cube outmaps): 1897 USO completions of the walk 13,18,12,16,9,17,1,6,0,4,5, 875 acyclic (B^2 among them), 0 Holt-Klee, legal candidate tie sets exactly {} (180), {(5,2)} (162), {(7,3)} (297), {(5,2),(7,3)} (236). sigma_5 = 17 has bit 2 = 0, sigma_7 = 6 has bit 2 = 1, so fs15:two-ties applies. The route's B^2 is the paper's translated by 1: s_route(v) = s_paper(v xor 1), and its walk is prop:b2-realised's 12,19,13,17,8,16,0,7,1,5,4 xor 1.

findings.defect: Correct and new, but the written proof is wrong at one step: 'redirect every edge into them to t_1 and t_0 respectively; ... afterwards every non-sink value lies in (0,1)'. Redirecting leaves the value-1 and value-0 vertices in place, and a surviving value-1 AVERAGE vertex is then the unique maximiser, so the TOP oracle returns it and the reduction fails. The vertices must be deleted (they are unreachable after the redirection). The route's code does delete them, so this is a writeup slip, not a mathematical error. Separately, the result is by the route's own admission a seventh target-equivalent reformulation, i.e. a blocked route under rule 4.
findings.evidence: t_top.py: 'keep = [v for v in range(n) if 0 < w[v] < 1]' and the collapse map only ever emits indices of kept vertices -- the code deletes. The LaTeX in fs15:top does not. Re-ran the reduction on a fresh seed (t_top.py 7 400): 197 correct, 0 wrong. The arithmetic checks out: r=2a+2, m=r+2, both chain tops exceed 1-2^{-(r+1)} > 1-2^{-a}, and val(q)-val(p)=2^{-r} is impossible since distinct values differ by at least 2^{-2a} > 2^{-r}.

findings.defect: Two standard devices are used without acknowledgement, both of which frontier.tex itself attributes. The perturbation obj + eps*c of a degenerate LP objective is the textbook lexicographic perturbation; the paper names Charnes and Dantzig-Orden-Wolfe for it in lem:tie-perturb's proof. And the separability hypothesis is Gordan's alternative, which the paper names; the route cites only 'the separating hyperplane theorem'. Holt-Klee and Gaertner-Morris-Ruest ARE properly attributed by the route. From memory, unchecked against the sources.
findings.evidence: frontier.tex lem:tie-perturb proof: 'the lexicographic perturbation of a degenerate objective, a textbook device (from memory: Charnes; Dantzig, Orden and Wolfe)'. The prose after prop:no-linear-tiebreak: 'This is the shape Gordan's alternative predicts'. fs15:run-hk's proof names neither.

findings.defect: The sampling figures (15000 one-player normal forms at m=3 den 8; 4000 at m=4 den 8) do not vary the parameter the question turns on, namely RUN LENGTH: every sampled run, and the exhibited instance's own run, has length at most 2-4, far below h*_HK(4)=6. So the reported rarity is uninformative about whether the configuration can occur on a long run, which is the entire gap. The route does say the instance's run is 'well under h*_HK(4)=6' but presents the frequencies without this caveat, where frontier.tex states it explicitly for its own analogous test.
findings.evidence: frontier.tex after prop:no-linear-tiebreak: '...was tested on 4320 runs of 191 random degenerate games at m=4,5 without ever failing; but those runs have length at most 4, far below the ceilings, so this is a report and not evidence.' The route's fs15:escape-remark reports 1-in-15000 and 1-in-4000 without the corresponding sentence.

findings.defect: An immediate two-line corollary of lem:alphabet-cover, which the route itself says should be cited rather than reproved -- correctly, and it is listed as a result anyway. The bound lambda_i >= 2^{1-i} is the letter-side form of thm:alphabet-denominator's D(G) <= 2^{k-2}. No defect, but no content either.
findings.evidence: lem:alphabet-cover (frontier.tex line 2446) gives lambda = (lambda_i + lambda_j)/2 with lambda_i < lambda < lambda_j for every interior letter; with 1 the only letter above nu this yields nu = (1+lambda)/2 >= 1/2 and lambda_i >= lambda_{i-1}/2 directly.

findings.defect: The inverse parametrisation -- fix the value vectors, solve linearly for the rows -- is the standard inverse-optimization / inverse-reinforcement-learning move (for a fixed policy the constraints making it optimal are linear in the rewards; Ng-Russell, from memory, unchecked against the source). It is also already the design method of the round-15 gadget route recorded in prop:b2-realised, which succeeded on the very instance fs15's outer search failed on. The route attributes neither.
findings.evidence: prop:b2-realised proof, frontier.tex line ~4830: 'The game was designed by the round-15 gadget route ... and its rows were fixed by exact linear programming over the normal form.' The route's own logs (b4_k1_*.log, b4_k2_*.log, g4_k2_*.log) plateau without converging, including on the G-sharp calibration target.
